scholarships.title: Harvard College Need-Based Financial Aid (International Students)

existing.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office at Harvard College provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students regardless of their ability to pay. Financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students; because international students are not eligible for federal funding, the College applies its own job and scholarship money. For families with income of $100,000 or below and typical assets, aid covers all billed expenses including tuition, fees, food, housing, health insurance if needed, travel between campus and home, and $2,000 start-up and launch grants. Families with income up to $200,000 receive free tuition plus aid for additional costs. Aid is need-blind with respect to admission.
eligibility: Any applicant or admitted Harvard College student, regardless of country of residence or citizenship status
International students are eligible on the same basis as American students
Admitted students may apply for aid; Harvard states it cannot track aid materials for prospective students until admission
Current students reapply each academic year
existing.eligibility_summary: All Harvard College applicants and admitted students, regardless of country of residence or citizenship status, may apply for need-based financial aid. International students are eligible on the same basis as U.S. students, though they cannot receive federal funding.
benefits: All billed expenses covered for families with income of $100,000 or below and typical assets
Full tuition covered for families with income of $200,000 or below and typical assets (Free Tuition Plus)
Travel allowance between campus and home
coverage: $2,000 start-up grant in the first year
$2,000 launch grant in the junior year
Travel costs between campus and home
requirements: Apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission
Provide information about family income and assets, outside awards and any unusual or changed financial circumstances
File the CSS Profile; international families may use the alternate paper process in exceptional circumstances
documents: FAFSA (for U.S. citizens and permanent residents)
Parents' and student's income tax documents
Business/farm supplement, cash flow statement or federal tax non-filer statement where applicable
application_method: Apply for financial aid at the same time as the admission application
Submit the CSS Profile and, where applicable, the FAFSA
International students in exceptional circumstances may use Harvard's alternate paper financial aid process
existing.selection_notes: All Harvard financial aid is awarded on the basis of demonstrated need; there are no academic, athletic or merit-based awards. Applying for aid does not affect admission chances.
existing.best_fit: Students from families with modest or moderate income who cannot pay Harvard's full cost of attendance.
existing.notes: Harvard states that twenty-four percent of students pay nothing to attend and more than half receive need-based scholarships. Ken Griffin's 2014 gift of $125 million underpins the current programme. Harvard expects students to cover $3,500 in personal expenses per academic year, usually through work-study hours.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle tied to Harvard's Restrictive Early Action (November 1), Regular Decision (February 1) and Transfer (March 1) admission rounds; current students reapply by May 1.
existing.deadline_display: Harvard College states: "Prospective Students: November 1st, for Restrictive Early Action candidates. February 1st, for Regular Decision candidates. March 1st, for Transfer candidates. Current Students: May 1st."
existing.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid programme (not a merit scholarship)
